facts.text: Agriculture and ag-related businesses account for nearly 20% of GDP in the Lethbridge region, home to Cavendish Farms, Maple Leaf Foods, Richardson International and McCain Foods.
Lethbridge's manufacturing sector generates more than $1.2 billion in annual sales and employs about 4,800 people with a payroll exceeding $185 million.
The Agri-Food Hub and Trade Centre at Exhibition Park creates 50 full-time permanent positions and is expected to contribute more than $90 million every year to the regional economy.
Alberta Health Services is Lethbridge's largest employer, with the University of Lethbridge, Lethbridge College and Sunrise Poultry, the largest private-sector employer, also major employers.

overview: Lethbridge grew 6.1 per cent between 2016 and 2021 to reach 98,406 residents, faster than the provincial average. Households reported a median total income of $82,000 in 2020, and 40,225 occupied dwellings sit within 121.12 square kilometres, so the customer base is compact and steadily expanding.

The economy rests on agri-food, which accounts for nearly 20 per cent of regional GDP, together with health care and post-secondary institutions. For a local business, that means a stable base of institutional payrolls, a large farm and food-processing supply chain to sell into, and new residents arriving each year who have not yet picked their providers.

byService.lead-generation: Lead generation in Lethbridge can pair consumer campaigns for a population that grew 6.1 per cent from 2016 to 2021 with business-to-business outreach to the agri-food processors that dominate the regional economy.
byService.seo: Because Lethbridge is compact at 121.12 square kilometres, SEO should focus on west, south and north side neighbourhood terms and on southern Alberta searches from surrounding farm communities.
byService.website-development: A Lethbridge website should speak to households with a median 2020 income of $82,000 while also presenting credentials clearly enough for institutional and agri-food buyers.
byService.branding: Lethbridge branding should reflect the city's agricultural roots and university character, since nearly 20 per cent of regional GDP comes from agriculture and residents value practical, local credibility.
